app/nuxt.config.ts:1-17 — only long-stable config keys: compatibilityDate, css, runtimeConfig.public, app.head.htmlAttrs
app/app/pages/index.vue:17 — useAsyncData with key + handler, stable since Nuxt 3

grep for experimental|unstable|preview|beta|canary across app/app — zero matches
reach.rationale: The app reaches for nothing experimental and nothing even recently stabilized beyond the Nuxt 4 app/ directory layout, which has been the framework default since 4.0 (July 2025) and is simply the idiomatic structure now. Every API in use (useAsyncData, useHead, defineNuxtPlugin, runtimeConfig, NuxtLink/NuxtPage, $fetch) is long-stable.

evidence: app/app/utils/poke.ts:1-257 — all data access centralized in one utils module behind fetchApi/fetchRecord wrappers
app/app/plugins/api-base.ts:1-4 — the only place runtime config is read, injected via a single plugin
app/app/components/NotFound.vue:4-5 — direct event.node.res.statusCode mutation is repeated in 5 files but is a one-line, easily replaceable idiom
containment.rationale: There is nothing experimental to contain; the app's data layer is already wrapped in a single module and plugin, so any future swap would be trivial.

evidence: app/nuxt.config.ts — no experimental flags, no future.compatibility opt-ins
app/app/pages/[...path].vue:1-3 — 404 handling via a plain catch-all page, the standard routing feature
justification.rationale: No experimental, preview, or canary APIs are used at all, so the justification criterion is trivially satisfied.

findings.issue: 404 status is set by mutating event.node.res.statusCode directly (repeated in moves/[name].vue:36-37, pokemon/[name].vue:172-173, types/[name].vue:45-46, abilities/[name].vue:31-32) instead of throwing createError({ statusCode: 404 }). This relies on the h3 v1 event shape (event.node), which Nuxt 4.6's new nuxt/server portable RequestEvent surface is designed to abstract away ahead of h3 v2/Nuxt 5.
findings.suggestion: Use throw createError({ statusCode: 404 }) in the data loaders (Nuxt's supported way to render the error page with a 404 status), or at minimum centralize the status-set in the NotFound component's single call site rather than five script blocks.

summary: This is a deliberately conservative app: it uses only long-stable Nuxt 4 APIs (useAsyncData, useHead, defineNuxtPlugin, runtimeConfig, $fetch, file-based routing) pinned to the current stable release, with zero experimental flags or unstable imports. Nothing experimental is relied on, so there is no breakage risk from framework churn beyond ordinary version upgrades. The only forward-looking nit is the hand-rolled event.node.res.statusCode 404 handling spread across five pages, which is stable today but bypasses the framework's createError path.
